chapter: 1977: Kansas City honor and the piano
title: Tributes at the roundtable, Jo Jones's speech, and missing the Yale event
summary: Basie recalls the press roundtable where Jo Jones and Sweets Edison spoke, and says health tests kept him from the Yale event.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Did anybody make a tribute to you from your cronies? Anybody talk about their years with you?
At the party, at the thing in Kansas City?
Yes.

Oh, yes, they had a little press -- oh, yes, Ozzie Davis was there and he (inaudible) and oh, yes, they had a little thing one afternoon, a round table and it was for the press and a few visitors were there that were asking a lot of things.
Did anybody make -- you know, speak about, were there any talks?
Oh, yes.
I guess at the University, would that be where it was.

No, it was at this little roundtable thing. Everybody was at the table and so everybody spoke, but -- oh, yes, a very famous guy, he was one of the first members of the band, Joe Jones, of the original originally with the rhythm section. I spoke and he spoke and Sweets Edison, you know, he had his
thing going.
What did he say?

Oh, boy, he would do his long thing. Then of course, Joe Jones, I mean, gee whiz, this guy, he's an ambassador. He's so great. You should Used to try to get him for some of I mean, no kidding, he'd knock you out. He really laid it right down. your things down there, to speak. (inaudible) Everybody wide that was open while he was speaking, just beautiful. I didn't know Jo could [speak] like that.
Is it true that journalists out there thought he was Mr. Basie?
Thought who, Joe was. [Think] They couldn't be positive. (Inaudible) You heard that --
What can I tell you? Let's see, what was the most moving thing that somebody told you? What was the most moving thing that one of the guys said, do you remember? Anything that brought you back?
Truthfully, each thing that each one of these guys when they spoke (inaudible) I cannot put my finger on the one which meant the greatest to me. (Inaudible) They were so marvelous.
Buck was there too, I guess.
Oh, I'm glad you mentioned that. You see. Oh, yes, my man. Oh, yeah, Bucket was there.
Okay. Then you didn't do the Yale thing because you went home to rest.
Yeah, I got home but then I had my
appointment there, had all my tests and everything done there and it was a little hard for me to get back and do this -- and it hurt me too, because I really did want to do this thing.
: Well, again, another time.
Oh, yes, I hope there's another time for me.
There shall be, I'm sure, I'm sure.
